bullets.title: MSFT: Copilot Super App + usage-based billing launch; $570 PT upgrades
bullets.body: Microsoft launched Copilot with three new agents (Home, Code, Autopilot) and a usage-based billing shift for agentic workloads. Stifel upgraded to Buy ($575 PT), Oppenheimer raised to $570, citing Azure capacity outpacing supply and potential 46-50% CC growth in near quarters. The Super App bundles M365 Copilot with FinOps controls for AI spend.

bullets.title: META: Muse AI agent hits #1 App Store; JPM raises PT to $920 on ~$30T agentic TAM
bullets.body: Meta's Muse personal AI agent reached 2.8M downloads in 12 days, topping the App Store and outpacing early ChatGPT metrics. JPMorgan raised its PT to $920 (26x 2028E EPS of $35.44), citing agent-to-agent monetization potential and Shopify/PayPal payment integrations. Amazon blocked Muse from its platform. Meta shares surged ~11% Monday, gaining ~$200B in market cap, and are up ~33% in September.

bullets.title: AKAM: $11.6B Anthropic deal transforms earnings story; analyst PTs range $158–$185
bullets.body: Akamai announced a 7-year, $11.6B take-or-pay contract with Anthropic for CPU-based cloud infrastructure (expandable to $20B), requiring ~$5.5B capex. Revenue ramps in 2H27 to $150-300M for FY27 and ~$1.7B run-rate by end-2028. Oppenheimer (OW, $180 PT), D.A. Davidson (Buy, $185), and Piper (OW, $158) all see CIS segment as transformative re-rating catalyst.

bullets.title: NVDA: CEO NDR bullish on 2x chip demand; Colossus 2 GPU orders may double
bullets.body: Jensen Huang stated AI should be developed 'as fast as we can' and projected NVDA will sell twice as many chips next year. Separately, SpaceX's Colossus 2 is reportedly set to double NVDA GPU orders QoQ (~660K incremental chips, ~$18B). NVDA forward P/E sits at ~16-17x, a decade low, while stock screen as a consensus long near 5Y lows in HF positioning. Bullish trend breakout signals confirmed.

bullets.title: AMD: Hits $1T market cap for first time on CPU/agentic AI demand surge; INTC, ARM rallied 12-14%
bullets.body: AMD broke above $600 post-split and crossed $1T market cap, +9-10% Monday, driven by Muse-related CPU demand read-throughs and agentic AI workloads (which require 3-4 GPUs per CPU vs. 7-8 for training). Intel +12% and ARM +14-17% also rallied sharply. Multiple analysts cite this as a structural shift in the semiconductor narrative from GPU-only to CPU+GPU.

bullets.title: ORCL: Force majeure on Project Jupiter raises AI infrastructure credit concerns
bullets.body: Oracle issued a force majeure notice on its 2.45 GW New Mexico data center (Project Jupiter), seeking to defer payments if delivery is delayed past 2028. Gas pipeline permit was denied twice; project debt trading below 90¢. Oracle claims Jupiter remains on schedule; Bloom Energy (which has a $1.25B EBITDA exposure) says it has contractual protections. KeyBanc maintains OW ($300 PT) but flags Oracle's weakest cash position among hyperscalers. MS and JPM caution on overhang.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Downgraded to underweight at KeyBanc ($18 PT); MS cuts to $27 on broadband headwinds
bullets.body: KeyBanc cut Comcast to Underweight from Sector Weight with an $18 PT, projecting 3Q broadband net adds of -140K vs. -119K consensus, with FWA/fiber/Starlink eroding share and ARPU under pressure. Morgan Stanley separately lowered its PT from $29 to $27, estimating AI agent disruption risk and forecasting broadband losses of -7.5% y/y in 3Q26.

bullets.title: MU: Earnings 9/30 with consensus $31.45 EPS / $50.97B revenue; UBS models $212+ through-cycle EPS
bullets.body: Micron reports Wednesday Sept 30 post-close. UBS modeled CY27/28/29 EPS of $212/$277/$219, well above street, driven by DRAM tightness (supply fulfillment ~60%, server SSD demand >100% YoY) and imminent mega-buybacks once CHIPS Act restrictions expire Dec 9. Michael Burry disclosed increased MU shorts. ITC instituted investigation against MU on NLST DRAM patents.

bullets.title: MRVL: MS raises PT to $268; Investor Day Oct 6 seen as catalyst on $40B+ 2030 revenue path
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised Marvell's PT to $268 (from $246) ahead of the Oct 6 Investor Day, where management is expected to guide FY2030 revenue to $40B+ led by Google custom silicon and Scale-Up AI networking. Seaport initiated Buy at $270. Oppenheimer noted interconnect revenue tracking >70% YoY growth (vs. prior 50% estimate), with Scale-Across sales projected to top $1B next year.

bullets.title: META/AMZN: AMZN blocks Muse agent; agentic commerce disruption narrative intensifies
bullets.body: Amazon blocked Meta's Muse from accessing Amazon.com, citing credential handling and unauthorized access concerns. Analysts see this as Amazon protecting its retail media auction and customer data. In contrast, Shopify (+7%), PayPal, and Expedia announced partnerships with Muse. Morgan Stanley estimates ~$30T consumer spend addressable through agentic offerings, with AMZN, SHOP, AAPL as winners and EXPE/BKNG at risk.

bullets.title: T: BNP Paribas Exane upgrades to Outperform ($30 PT) on fiber convergence and wireless tailwinds
bullets.body: BNP Paribas Exane upgraded AT&T to Outperform from Neutral, raising its PT to $30 from $26, citing AT&T as the best way to play wireless tailwinds from fiber convergence. Morgan Stanley raised T's PT from $27 to $28 and views AT&T as second-least impacted carrier from AI agent disruption, with 38M+ fiber passings supporting bundled convergence.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: Paramount settles California antitrust; merger path to close in ~2 weeks
bullets.body: Paramount Skydance reached settlement with California AG and coalition of state AGs on the WBD acquisition, requiring $1.5B in California production investment, 30+ movies per year (with $30M penalty per film shortfall), and 5-year separate cable negotiations. WBD +11%, PSKY +4-6%. Morgan Stanley raised PSKY PT to $11.50, reiterating OW, citing clear path to $6B+ in synergies and 240M+ streaming subscribers.

bullets.title: CIEN: Upgraded to Outperform by Evercore ISI ($550 PT from $375); supply-constrained backlog
bullets.body: Evercore upgraded Ciena to Outperform with a $550 PT, projecting 30%+ annual sales growth and $25+ EPS by FY2029, supported by AI-driven optical networking demand expanding 24% CAGR to $52B. ECOC 2026 takeaways showed Ciena's Hyper-Rail opportunity with several hundred million dollars of expected 2027 revenue; supply constraints mean 2027 guidance is effectively a floor.

bullets.title: COHR: Launches PhotonLink integrated optics platform; 10+ CPO and NPO engagements
bullets.body: Coherent launched PhotonLink at ECOC 2026, an end-to-end integrated optics platform spanning CPO, NPO, and chip-to-chip connections, targeting $30B+ SAM by 2030 (up from $15B). Management disclosed 10+ CPO engagements, 10+ NPO engagements, and a secured NPO LTA. Scale-out CPO revenue begins Q4 CY26, scale-up H2 CY27. MS maintains Equal Weight ($375 PT).

bullets.title: TSEM: Mizuho initiates Outperform at $300 PT on silicon photonics and RF infrastructure growth
bullets.body: Mizuho initiated Tower Semiconductor at Outperform with a $300 PT, citing SiPho foundry market growing at 60% CAGR to $8.5B by 2029 and RF infrastructure revenue growing at 76% CAGR to reach 77% of total revenue. EPS projected to grow 7x to $16.51 by FY29. Independent analyst also initiated at Outperform (same $300 PT).

bullets.title: LITE: Bullish at ECOC; NPO LTA expected, 1.6T ramp faster than expected
bullets.body: Lumentum emerged constructive from ECOC 2026, with supply constraints potentially running further behind demand than pre-conference expectations. Management is sole-sourced on a higher port-count inference SKU; NPO LTA announcement expected. AI transceiver demand updated to 180M units C27 and 245M in C28. TX GMs expected to push to 30%+. Jefferies (BUY, $325 PT) and Citi remain bullish.

bullets.title: DKNG: Predictions opex raised to $400-500M (was $200-300M), cutting 2026 EBITDA 20%
bullets.body: Oppenheimer revised 2026 DraftKings EBITDA estimate 20% lower to $548M due to higher Predictions investment spend ($400-500M vs. prior $200-300M). 2026 EBITDA midpoint now well below prior guidance of $700-900M. Massachusetts regulator also launched examination of how betting companies use AI. Stock underperformed S&P by 20% since late August on this risk.

bullets.title: NOK: Jefferies upgrades to Buy (€13.80 PT); InP capacity expansion a key catalyst
bullets.body: Jefferies upgraded Nokia to Buy with a €13.80 PT (49% upside) following ECOC meetings. Nokia booked ~€5B in AI optical orders since 2025 and is ramping a second InP fab in San Jose that will increase capacity 20x+ when fully ramped. Nokia 2027-28 EPS is ~21% above consensus. Seaport and JPM also cite Nokia's IP Network strength (40% of 2Q26 orders) and competitive InP integration as differentiated.

bullets.title: CRDO: 115% YoY revenue growth but stock sold off; 4Q earnings reset expectations
bullets.body: Credo Semiconductor posted 115% YoY revenue growth but experienced a post-earnings selloff. Multiple analysts maintain OW/Buy ratings at investor meetings at OCP 2026 (Oct 13). Stock bounced off bottom trendline in intraday action. Hedgeye bullish trend breakout signal confirmed on CRDO. ECOC takeaways were positive on 800G-to-1.6T ramp positioning.

bullets.title: CRWV: JPM upgrades to Overweight ($125 PT) on GPU pricing power and margin expansion
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded CoreWeave to Overweight with a Dec-27 PT of $125 (42% upside), citing July GPU pricing increases of 25% across SKUs, short-term contract pricing 3x longer-term rates, and operating margins expanding from ~1% in FQ1 to low-teens% by FQ4. UBS also initiated Buy at $120, noting channel checks on reliability and performance differentiation. Jefferies called CRWV a top AI conference pick.
